projects.title: BubuProtect
projects.tagline: On-device Android password vault: two encryption layers, keys wiped the moment it locks
projects.summary: A password vault is only as safe as its weakest path: a copied database file, a memory dump, a look-alike app asking for autofill. I built an Android vault for logins, cards, notes, IDs and Wi-Fi keys with a defense for each, everything kept on the device and one network call: a breach check that never sends the password.
highlights: Encrypted every secret twice: SQLCipher over the database file, then AES-GCM per field, bound to its entry and column so copied or swapped ciphertext fails as tampering
Wrapped one 256-bit root key three independent ways (a biometric Keystore key, the passphrase through PBKDF2 at 210,000 iterations, a paper recovery code), so losing one never loses the vault
Closed the database and wiped the keys from memory on every lock, so a locked vault can't be read from a heap dump
Made autofill trust an app's signing certificate, not its package name, so a sideloaded look-alike never receives a bank's password
Built a device check of 10 local probes (root, debugging, network interception and more) and a DNS-only VPN that blocks ad trackers
Covered the crypto, autofill, CSV import, OTP and breach-check code with 208 JVM unit tests in 22 test classes

engineering.architecture: Single Gradle module: ui (Compose screens, StateFlow ViewModels), domain (models, VaultRepository interface), data (Room DAOs over SQLCipher), session (holds keys and the open database only while unlocked) and core feature packages for crypto, autofill, security probes, shield, OTP, backup and import. Koin wires it. No backend; the one network call is a k-anonymous Pwned Passwords lookup.

decisions.title: One key, three independent locks
decisions.detail: A 256-bit root key is wrapped by a hardware Keystore key (biometric per use, destroyed if a new fingerprint is enrolled), by PBKDF2-SHA512 at 210,000 iterations and by a paper recovery code, so no single failure loses the vault.

decisions.title: Two encryption layers, bound per field
decisions.detail: SQLCipher encrypts the database file; AES-GCM then seals each credential column with the entry id and column name as associated data, so copied or swapped ciphertext fails as tampering instead of leaking.

decisions.title: Locked means the keys are gone
decisions.detail: On lock, VaultSession closes the database, zeroes the derived passphrase and wipes the root key, so a locked vault cannot be read from a heap dump. Re-entry needs real authentication.

decisions.title: DNS-only VPN for ad tracking
decisions.detail: The VpnService routes a single /32 fake DNS address, so only DNS enters the tunnel: no userspace TCP stack, other traffic never touched and no way to carry user traffic anywhere.

projects.title: Vistago
projects.tagline: Android travel app with on-device sign translation and AI that reroutes when a model fails
projects.summary: A travel app is needed most where it works worst: abroad, offline, in front of a sign you can't read. Vistago plans trips, translates signs live through the camera and keeps trip memories, with Room as the source of truth and on-device fallbacks for planning and translation. Its AI runs on free models picked at call time, so a retired or rate-limited model reroutes instead of failing.
highlights: Ran live camera translation on device with ML Kit across five script families, tracking lines frame to frame so labels hold still instead of flickering
Built a model router that discovers free OpenRouter models at call time, benches rate-limited models and reroutes around retired ones, so no model name is hard-coded
Kept Room as the source of truth through 12 schema versions and 11 hand-written migrations with no destructive fallback, so an update never wipes a traveler's trips
Kept the domain layer pure Kotlin (82 files, zero Android imports) and covered the app with 800 JVM unit tests and 15 instrumented tests

engineering.architecture: Single Gradle module layered as Compose UI, then 16 ViewModels exposing StateFlow and sealed UI states, then a pure-Kotlin domain layer (models, repository interfaces, use cases, LLM routing rules; zero android imports), then a data layer (Room, OpenRouter, ML Kit, Supabase, WorkManager). Koin wires the graph and injects a named IO dispatcher. Room is the source of truth; Supabase is optional best-effort sync behind the same interfaces.

decisions.title: Self-healing model router
decisions.detail: No model is hard-coded. The router discovers free OpenRouter models at call time, benches a model for a cooldown after a 429, treats retired models as a reroute and tags every reply with which model answered.

decisions.title: Degrades instead of breaking
decisions.detail: Koin picks implementations at startup: without an API key, trip planning and interest suggestions fall back to on-device versions, and live camera translation runs entirely on device with ML Kit, so the app stays usable offline.

decisions.title: Local-first data, swappable remote
decisions.detail: Room owns the experience offline, at schema v12 with 11 explicit migrations and no destructive fallback. Supabase sync and an Edge Function proxy sit behind repository interfaces so AI secrets never ship in the APK.

decisions.title: Live OCR that holds still
decisions.detail: Raw recognition jitters, drops out and misreads glyphs, so a naive overlay blinks. A tested tracker matches lines across frames, eases them into place and paints a label only after repeated reads.

projects.title: Seventh J
projects.tagline: Gallery app for Android, iOS and web, with a 3D sculpture renderer in shared Kotlin
projects.summary: An inventory and dealer-floor app for a Makati art gallery, built once in Compose Multiplatform for Android, iOS and the web. Instead of a 3D engine per platform for one turntable, I wrote a small software renderer in common Kotlin, and every screen shares one codebase with no Android imports. It runs on sample data while the data layer is built.
projects.disclaimer: A concept build: I used a real Makati art gallery to show what I can develop. It isn't their official app as of now, and their name and brand belong to them.
highlights: Wrote a software 3D renderer in common Kotlin (rotate, project, cull, depth-sort, shade, fill) that turns about 1,000 faces per sculpture with zero allocation per frame
Painted a Starry Night splash from 960 strokes in one flow field: 420 short sky dashes and 540 long threads that spiral into the pixels of the gallery's mark
Shared every screen across Android, iOS and the web: 78 common files, zero android.* imports, platform needs behind expect/actual
Kept the back stack restorable on iOS and Wasm, where reflection is unavailable, with serializable Navigation 3 destinations and explicit polymorphic serializers
Budgeted the animation per platform: the splash plays once on Android and iOS, and is skipped on the web, on warm start and under reduced motion
Covered UI state, inventory, sales and the sculpture meshes with 35 shared tests; CI builds the release APK and compiles for Wasm on every push

engineering.architecture: A KMP library, :shared, holds every screen in commonMain; :androidApp, :webApp (Wasm and JS) and an Xcode iosApp are thin entry points. Each screen splits into a stateless Content composable, a thin Screen wrapper and a multiplatform ViewModel exposing StateFlow of a sealed UiState. Platform differences go through expect/actual. Data is sample and in-memory for now; DI and a database are planned, not built.

decisions.title: One UI codebase, no Android leaks
decisions.detail: commonMain has zero android.* imports. Platform needs such as reduced motion are expect/actual with Android, iOS, JS and Wasm implementations, so all three apps run the same UI code.

decisions.title: Reflection-free navigation
decisions.detail: Destinations are a @Serializable sealed interface on Navigation 3 with explicit polymorphic serializers, because reflection is unavailable on iOS and Wasm and the back stack must still restore there.

decisions.title: Animation budgeted per platform
decisions.detail: The 960-stroke Starry Night splash plays once per process on Android and iOS only. It is skipped on the web, on warm start and under reduced motion, because that many canvas strokes would stall a browser tab.

decisions.title: One software renderer, not three engines
decisions.detail: Filament on Android, SceneKit on iOS and three.js on the web would be three engines and three sets of bugs for one turntable, so one painter's-algorithm pass over about 1,000 quads runs in common Kotlin.

projects.title: Calm Escape Premier
projects.tagline: Multi-tenant spa booking where the database itself makes double bookings impossible
projects.summary: Each spa gets its own booking site and staff back office, customers book from iOS and Android apps, and all of them share one schedule. With Kotlin apps, a TypeScript website and customers booking at the same moment, I put the rules in one place: Postgres enforces tenant isolation, availability and double-booking prevention, covered by 184 database tests.
projects.disclaimer: A concept build: I used a real spa business to show what I can develop. It isn't their official app as of now, and their name and brand belong to them.
highlights: Made double booking impossible at the database: exclusion constraints stop a therapist or room being booked twice, even when two requests race
Isolated every spa's data with Row Level Security on all 19 tables (58 policies) and composite tenant keys, so a booking can't point at another spa's therapist or room
Wrote the booking, availability, cancellation and voucher rules once, as Postgres functions that both the Kotlin apps and the TypeScript web call, so they can't disagree
Served every spa from one Next.js codebase on its own subdomain or custom domain, server-rendered and cached, in one of three designs
Gave staff a back office with monthly sales, a menu and membership editor, and promo bundles with a live phone and web preview
Tested it at three layers: 184 pgTAP database tests, 346 Vitest tests and 42 Kotlin tests, with CI checking migrations, SQL lint and that the generated types match the schema

engineering.architecture: Two thin front ends over one database. Tenant isolation (Row Level Security), double-booking prevention (exclusion constraints), slot availability and booking and voucher RPCs live once in Postgres, so Kotlin and TypeScript cannot disagree. mobile/shared holds models, supabase-kt repositories, ViewModels with StateFlow and the Compose UI for Android and iOS. Next.js routes by host and server-renders cached spa pages. Dependencies are passed by constructor; no DI framework.

decisions.title: Business rules live in Postgres
decisions.detail: Mobile is Kotlin and web is TypeScript, so availability, booking, cancellation and voucher rules are SQL functions over RPC and access is RLS. Both clients only render and call the same functions, with stable error hints.

decisions.title: Double-booking impossible, even under races
decisions.detail: EXCLUDE USING gist constraints on bookings stop a therapist or room being booked twice at the database. Voucher claim limits are enforced inside a claim_voucher RPC; customers cannot write claims directly.

decisions.title: Tenant-safe foreign keys
decisions.detail: Every spa-owned row carries tenant_id, and child rows reference parents by composite (id, tenant_id) keys, so a booking cannot point at another spa's service, therapist, room or location.

decisions.title: KMP for apps, server-rendered web
decisions.detail: The team knows Kotlin, so apps are KMP + Compose Multiplatform. Flutter and Compose for web draw to a canvas with weak SEO, so spa sites are server-rendered Next.js (ADR 0001).

projects.title: The Eagle's Watch
projects.tagline: Civic app that labels where every public-works figure came from, on Android and the web
projects.summary: A progress figure with no source can't be checked. The Eagle's Watch lists Philippine public works with their contracts, schedules, progress and documents, and labels every figure with how it was established. It is a design preview on ten fictional records, built so a live government source plugs in behind one interface without changing a screen.
highlights: Made provenance part of the data model: every figure carries one of four labels (Verified, Agency-reported, Community-reported, Not available), and a missing value reads "Not on file" instead of a guess
Kept reported progress, independently checked progress, funds disbursed and contract time as separate meters, so one is never passed off as another
Built search and a filter sheet over six facets (status, type, level of government, province, agency, contract size) with live counts and four sort orders
Designed a report flow reachable from every screen: mostly taps, anonymous unless the citizen adds contact details, with a reference number for each report
Made status readable without color (five shapes plus labels), with text at 4.5:1 contrast or better and tap targets of at least 48dp
Shipped Android and the web from one Compose Multiplatform codebase, with icons and a Philippines locator map drawn in code instead of libraries

engineering.architecture: One composeApp module: a shared Compose UI in commonMain with thin Android, iOS and Wasm entry points. A ProjectRepository interface feeds a ProjectStore exposing a sealed LoadState (Loading, Ready, Failed) as Compose state with retry. CitizenState keeps the watchlist and reports on the device through expect/actual storage. Every figure in the domain model carries an Attribution: verification label, source and date. No DI framework.

decisions.title: Provenance is part of the data model
decisions.detail: Progress, parties, updates, photos and documents each carry an Attribution with one of four labels (Verified, Agency-reported, Community-reported, Not available). The UI never implies more than the label, and missing values read "Not on file".

decisions.title: A repository seam for live data
decisions.detail: The ten fictional records live only in SampleData.kt behind ProjectRepository. A live government source implements that interface and the screens do not change.

decisions.title: Status never depends on color
decisions.detail: Each of the five statuses has its own shape (outline, half disc, triangle, square, ticked disc) plus a label; text reads at 4.5:1 or better and every tap target is at least 48dp.

decisions.title: Glass that degrades gracefully
decisions.detail: Frosted surfaces use Haze backdrop blur where content scrolls underneath; on Android before 12, where the platform cannot blur, they fall back to a near-opaque tint.

projects.title: Pawffice
projects.tagline: Multiplayer 3D town on Mac and Android from one engine, with an AI crew that edits code
projects.summary: A shared 3D town where, on the Mac, a crew of AI cats takes your prompts and reads or edits the folders you connect. The hard parts were one three.js engine in both a Tauri desktop app and an Android app, NPCs synced without a game server and an agent working on real code with no shell while your API token never reaches the page.
highlights: Shipped one three.js engine to a Tauri Mac app and an Expo Android app by swapping a single IPC module; the phone build fails if desktop-only code slips in
Let the AI crew touch only the folders you connect: the page sends a project id, Rust resolves the path, no shell is ever offered and a cloned repo's hooks and MCP config are never loaded
Kept the Claude token out of the web page: Rust seals it with AES-256-GCM under an Argon2id key (64 MiB, 3 passes) and zeroizes it on sign-out
Synced shared NPCs between players with no game server: clients elect a host from Supabase Realtime presence, and it sends 4 delta frames a second to stay inside the free-plan message quota
Cut phone frame time from about 44 to 36 ms and triangles per frame from 1.57M to 0.77M with a measured quality tier (8 fur shells instead of 16, a 1024² shadow map), leaving desktop unchanged
Backed it with 730 automated tests (666 JavaScript, 64 Rust), 6 CI jobs with clippy warnings as errors and 30 architecture decision records

engineering.architecture: Dependencies point one way: phone, then desktop page, then engine. packages/cattown is a three.js engine whose rules (steering, physics, driving, network smoothing) sit in pure, unit-tested modules. The Pawffice page, plain JavaScript, mounts it and reaches its host through one ipc module: Tauri commands into Rust on the Mac, a swapped shim on the phone, where an Expo shell runs the page in a WebView. Supabase provides accounts and Realtime.

decisions.title: One engine, never a second
decisions.detail: The phone is an Expo/React Native shell around a WebView running the desktop page, rebuilt with esbuild and one swapped ipc module. A native 3D rewrite needs a new ADR; the build fails if Tauri code leaks in.

decisions.title: The API token never reaches the page
decisions.detail: Rust seals the Claude token with AES-256-GCM under an Argon2id key (64 MiB, 3 passes). It lives only in the Rust process, zeroized on sign-out; the web page gets back name and role only.

decisions.title: Shared NPCs with no game server
decisions.detail: Clients elect one NPC host from Realtime presence (oldest join wins), so every device agrees without a server. The host sends 4 delta frames a second to stay under Supabase's free-plan message quota; lockstep was rejected.

decisions.title: An AI crew with no shell
decisions.detail: The crew gets read tools, or read and edit tools in Edit mode, and never a shell, so it cannot run commands, install packages or push. Paths are looked up in Rust, never taken from the page.

projects.tagline: One Compose codebase for web and Android, a crawlable HTML twin and a tested backend
projects.summary: The page you're reading. One Compose Multiplatform UI runs in your browser through Kotlin/WebAssembly and in an Android app that doubles as my inbox, while the build renders the same JSON to crawlable HTML that paints first, so search engines, screen readers and browsers without WebAssembly GC get everything too. engineering.architecture: composeApp runs in one-way layers: UI, ViewModel, repository, parser, model. All content is one JSON file, validated by the same parser in the app and in the build task that renders the crawlable HTML. The browser paints that HTML first and swaps to the Wasm canvas once Compose has drawn. androidApp wraps the same UI; a Cloudflare Worker over D1 serves visits, notes and messages.

decisions.title: Crawlable HTML first, canvas second
decisions.detail: A canvas is invisible to search engines and screen readers, and the runtime is megabytes. The build renders the same JSON to HTML, which paints first and stays the page where WasmGC is missing.

decisions.title: Clips decoded one frame at a time
decisions.detail: Skia's Codec decodes animated WebP into one reusable bitmap inside the frame clock: about 1.2 MB a clip instead of 28 MB, and a shared gate allows one decode per display frame.

decisions.title: Content mistakes fail the build
decisions.detail: The app's parser also runs in Gradle, and tests check every listed image against its budget, so a broken link, missing alt text, an oversized image or a module cycle stops the deploy.

decisions.title: Inline scripts allowed by hash
decisions.detail: Each inline script on the static page is allowed by its SHA-256 hash in the Content-Security-Policy, which the build computes, so no 'unsafe-inline' is needed and an injected script cannot run.
